例句

  • Gold is seen as a stable asset when the economy is in decline.（经济下滑时，黄金被看作稳定的资产。）
  • Prices tend to fluctuate when supply is limited.（供应有限的时候，价格容易波动。）
  • Many families can't afford to save because of high inflation.（通胀太高，很多家庭存不下钱。）

过关标准：遮住中文看英文，能说出 22 个以上的意思，再挑 5 个自己造句。

BBC 6 Minute English：Why do people buy gold?（10 月 15 日）。音频和原文都已经放在页面里，不用打开 BBC 网站。

  1. 先把上面的听前生词过一遍。听不太懂的话，可以先点开下面的原文读懂再听。
  2. 第一遍不看文字，只听大意，回答开头的问题：人类历史上一共开采了多少黄金？a) 超过 5 万吨 b) 超过 10 万吨 c) 超过 20 万吨
  3. 第二遍点开下面的原文精听，听不出的地方暂停、倒回去并标出来。
  4. 第三遍挑 1 分钟左右的对话跟读，模仿语调和连读。
  5. 记住 6 个表达：asset（资产）、safe haven（避风港）、out of thin air（凭空）、alchemy（炼金术）、ethereal（虚无缥缈的）、a hankering for（很想要）。
点开看原文（难词带中文，点虚线词显示）

Georgie：Hi Phil.

Phil：Hi Georgie. I've got a question for you. Do you own anything made of gold?

Georgie：Well, at the moment I'm wearing a lot of gold-coloured jewellery珠宝首饰, but I'm not sure exactly how much of it is made of gold.

Phil：OK. I don't think I own anything made of gold. Beyond jewellery珠宝首饰 and other personal items, gold is bought and sold by investors and banks. The price of gold has always gone up and down涨涨跌跌, but in 2026 it reached its highest ever price. In this episode of 6 Minute English, we'll be talking about how gold became a valuable investment and asking the question, why do people buy gold?

Phil：Let's start with our quiz question, Georgie. Gold is a metal that's extracted or dug up挖出来 from under the ground in mines矿；矿井. But how much gold has been extracted from the earth? Is it:

a)    over 50,000 tonnes吨,

b)    over 100,000 tonnes吨, or

c)    over 200,000 tonnes吨?

Georgie：Phil, I have absolutely no idea, but I'm going to go with c) 200,000 tonnes吨.

Phil：OK. Well, we'll give you the answer at the end of the programme.

Georgie：OK Phil. So, we've been using gold for thousands of years, but why and how did it start?

Phil：Well, before money was paper or plastic or just numbers in your bank account, a lot of it was actually gold. And experts have discovered gold in coins that are thought to have been made in the 6th Century BC. So, gold coins were made and they were used because the metal was much easier to carry and trade than things like cattle牛（统称） or timber木材.

Georgie：OK. But now our money isn't literally字面上地；真正地 made of gold, so why is gold valuable?

Phil：It's a good question, but even though it isn't money, gold is still a financial asset, and an asset is something valuable that could be sold for money. And people buy gold in times of crisis危机在危机时期 because it's thought of as a safe investment. Let's listen to expert Suki Cooper explaining more to the BBC World Service.

Suki Cooper：Gold is a safe haven because it's not connected to one particular government or one particular economy or one particular market, so the fact that it's neutral中立的 means it's an asset that's perceived认为；看待 to be a store of value价值储存手段 over a longer term.

Phil：Suki describes gold as a safe haven, and a safe haven means something or somewhere that's protected from harm or danger, or in financial terms金融角度上, from a fall in value.

Georgie：Yes, Suki explains that, unlike dollars or pounds for example, gold is not connected to a particular country. It's neutral中立的.

Phil：And Georgie, because we get gold from mines矿；矿井, there's more or less a fixed amount. Unlike paper money, you can't just print more, as Catherine Schenk, professor of economic and social history, explains.

Catherine Schenk：It can't be created and fabricated制造；捏造 out of thin air through alchemy, and so this, sort of, controls the supply and sustains维持 an underlying根本的；潜在的 value behind the demand for gold.

 

Georgie：Catherine explains that gold can't be created out of thin air, an expression meaning making something from nothing.

Phil：As Catherine says, we don't make gold through alchemy. Alchemy is an ancient古代的 kind of chemistry that attempted尝试 to do impossible things, like turn ordinary普通的 metals into gold. And because we can't just magically make more gold, when lots of people want to buy gold, the price increases.

Georgie：OK. Understood. Now, Phil, at the start of this programme, you said that gold prices hit an all-time high历史最高点 in early 2026. So, what's going on?

Phil：Well, we mentioned that the price of gold increases in times of crisis危机在危机时期 because government banks want to buy more of it. And there has been a series of world events that have made government banks want to buy more gold, for example the wars in Ukraine and the Middle East, and in politics too, for example the US imposing强加；征收 tariffs关税 on international products. But since that peak顶峰 in January, the price has dropped a bit.

Georgie：OK. And does the fall in the price of gold mean that people won't want to invest in it in the future?

Phil：No. It's likely that the price will go up again. Experts believe that gold will always be an attractive investment during uncertain不确定的 times. Let's hear from market strategist策略师 John Reade.

John Reade：So much of the world we live in now is ethereal. It's... it's virtual虚拟的, it's online, it disappears, whereas gold is something solid, something dependable可靠的 and, you know, maybe something a little bit old fashioned老派的，过时的. And maybe it's a hankering for traditional values rather than what is super modern and super changeable.

Georgie：John says that much of the modern world is ethereal, meaning it doesn't seem real.

Phil：And in this ethereal world, people have a hankering for something that's solid and real, like gold. And the expression a hankering for means a strong desire for something.

Georgie：OK. Phil, I think it's time for the answer to your quiz question.

Phil：OK. Well, I asked how much gold has been mined from the ground to date.

Georgie：I said 200,000 tonnes吨.

Phil：And that is the correct answer! OK. Let's recap回顾；总结 the vocabulary we learnt in this programme, starting with asset. And an asset is something of financial value that can be sold for money.

Georgie：A safe haven is something or somewhere protected from harm or loss.

Phil：To make something out of thin air is an expression meaning to make something from nothing.

Georgie：Alchemy is a kind of ancient古代的 chemistry that attempted尝试 to do impossible things, like making gold from ordinary普通的 metals.

Phil：If something is ethereal, it doesn't seem real.

Georgie：And if you have a hankering for something, you have a strong desire for it.

Phil：Once again, our six minutes are up, and if you have a hankering for more practice, test what you've learned with the worksheet on our website. That's bbclearningenglish.com.

Georgie：Thank you for joining us. Goodbye.

Phil：Goodbye!

过关标准：不看原文能用中文说出这集讲了什么，6 个表达都知道意思，跟读那段能流利读下来。

小练习

  1. During a crisis, many people see gold as a ______ ______.（两个词，避风港）
  2. The price of oil can ______ a lot from month to month.
  3. If you spend more than your ______, you will soon run out of money.
  4. He's had a ______ ______ pizza all week.（很想吃）
点开看答案

开头那题选 c，超过 20 万吨。填空：1. safe haven 2. fluctuate 3. income（budget 也行）4. hankering for
